samples.summary: Internal table-cell paste bypasses the new `dropStaleStyleOffAll` cleanup
samples.evidence: `handleNativePaste` runs the cleanup only on the `data.blocks` branch (text-editor.ts:1258-1264). The sibling branch at text-editor.ts:1247-1253 (`data.tableCells` → `this.pasteTableCells(data.tableCells)`) comes from the same internal WAFFLEDOCS_MIME clipboard payload and `pasteTableCells` clones the cells verbatim (`cloneTableCells`, text-editor.ts:3743), so runs copied out of a Heading 6 keep their explicit `italic: false` and land in cell paragraphs whose named style never supplies italic — exactly the dead flag the diff's paste-path comment says the cleanup exists to remove. Fix belongs on the new code (add the same `dropStaleStyleOffAll()` call to the tableCells branch).

`mergeBlocks` (document.ts:379-382) calls `store.mergeBlock` + `refresh()` with no stale-flag cleanup, while `setBlockType` (document.ts:604-611) was given one. Backspace at the start of a Heading 6 merges its runs (which legitimately carry `italic: false` because the heading style supplies italic — see the diff's own test at test/model/document.test.ts:353) into the previous paragraph, where nothing supplies italic. The flag is then dead exactly as after a block-type change, blocks re-merging in `normalizeInlines`, and pins the run against later style redefinition. `deleteBackward` (document.ts:320) reaches this on the hottest editing path.

samples.summary: The cleanup write is a second Yorkie undo unit, so block-type change / style redefinition / paste now need two Cmd+Z
samples.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op — "Yorkie tracks undo units via doc.update()" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) — and `applyStyles` opens its own `this.doc.update(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806). `Doc.setBlockType` now issues `store.setBlockType` (one update) followed by `dropStaleStyleOff` → `store.applyStyles` (a second update); `afterNamedStyleChange` (view/editor.ts:1052) does the same after `writeStylesAndRematerialize` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2686, itself documented as "a single doc.update so the whole change is one undo unit"); the paste path does it after `insertBlocks`. The new comments claim the cleanup "undoes as one step" with the caller, which holds only for `MemDocStore`'s snapshot stack — under the collaborative store the first Cmd+Z undoes only the cleanup and leaves the heading/redefinition/paste in place.

samples.summary: `dropStaleStyleOffAll` on the paste path rewrites blocks that were never marked dirty for incremental layout
samples.evidence: The call at text-editor.ts:1264 sweeps every body, header, footer and (nested) cell block (`Doc.dropStaleStyleOffAll`, document.ts:497-518) and can rewrite runs far from the paste site, but the paste branch only calls `this.requestRender()` — no `markDirty`/`invalidateLayout` for those blocks. Every other caller of the sweep does invalidate (view/editor.ts:1057 `invalidateLayout()`), so the paste path can leave stale cached line boxes for a header/footer/table block whose runs were just re-merged.
searchedFor: grep markDirty/invalidateLayout in text-editor paste paths

samples.summary: Clearing a key re-merges runs in the local cache but not in the Yorkie Tree, so cache and CRDT diverge in inline structure
samples.evidence: The cache path `applyInlineStyleHelper` → `normalizeInlines` (block-helpers.ts:89) now merges the run back into its neighbour once the flag is cleared, but `applyStyleInTree` only removes empty inlines (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1963-1975) and never merges equal-attribute inline nodes. After a toggle-off the cached block has one run while the Tree still holds three; any remote patch or reload re-reads the split form via `treeNodeToBlock` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:434), so the #749 'single run restored' guarantee the new tests assert against `MemDocStore` does not hold in the collaborative store.

verdict.reason: The tableCells branch of handlePaste (text-editor.ts:1247-1253) really does return without calling dropStaleStyleOffAll, while the sibling blocks branch calls it (text-editor.ts:1264). A repo-wide grep for `dropStaleStyleOff` finds only three call sites — document.ts:611 (setBlockType), text-editor.ts:1264 (blocks paste), editor.ts:1056 (afterNamedStyleChange) — and pasteTableCells (text-editor.ts:3725-3793) reaches none of them, calling only cloneTableCells, normalizeTableMerges and updateBlockDirect/insertBlockAt. The payload preserves an explicit `false`: sanitizeInlineStyle keeps boolean keys valued `false` (clipboard.ts:137-140) and cloneTableCells copies inline styles verbatim (clipboard.ts:389-394). No counterexample exists, so I cannot refute. One correction to the reviewer's mechanism: pasteTableCells replaces whole cells and cloneTableCells preserves each block's type/headingLevel (clipboard.ts:389-391), and blockStyleId derives solely from type/headingLevel (named-styles.ts:99-114), so a Heading 6 run lands in a cloned Heading 6 block, not a paragraph — unlike insertBlocks, which splices pasted inlines into a differently-typed destination block (text-editor.ts:3626-3645). The gap is therefore narrower than described but still reachable: a copy taken before a named-style redefinition (editor.ts:1052-1056 sweeps the document, not the clipboard payload), or pasted into a document with different `styles`, strands the same dead `italic: false` the diff's own comment (text-editor.ts:1259-1263) says the cleanup exists to remove, and dropStaleStyleOffAll already walks nested cells (document.ts:505-509).

verdict.reason: No counterexample exists. `Doc.mergeBlocks` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:379-382) performs only `store.mergeBlock` + `refresh()`. A grep for `dropStaleStyleOff` across packages/docs/src yields exactly three invocation sites — document.ts:611 (setBlockType), view/editor.ts:1056 (afterNamedStyleChange), view/text-editor.ts:1264 (internal-clipboard paste) — none reachable from a merge. All eight callers of `mergeBlocks` (document.ts:320 deleteBackward; text-editor.ts:1959, 2005, 2030, 2076, 3243, 3345, 3411) go straight to cursor/render work; I read text-editor.ts:1955-1971 and 1974-1984 to confirm. No lower layer sanitises either: MemDocStore.mergeBlock (store/memory.ts:233-240) delegates to applyMergeBlocks (store/block-helpers.ts:344-350), which drops only `headingLevel` and calls normalizeInlines; YorkieDocStore.mergeBlock (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2246-2339) deep-clones the next block's inline nodes unchanged (its removeStyleByPath at 2285 only touches headingLevel); Doc.refresh (document.ts:123-125) is a pure re-read. The stranded flag is genuinely dead: normalizeInlines (block-helpers.ts:89-104) gates re-merge on inlineStylesEqual, which compares `italic` strictly (model/types.ts:479-499), so `false !== undefined`, and collectStaleStyleOff's own criterion (document.ts:540-546) matches exactly the post-merge state of a Heading-6 run moved into a paragraph. In-lane and blocking: the diff's cleanup establishes an invariant ("no run holds a boolean false no layer under it supplies") that an untouched, hot editing path (Backspace at block start, document.ts:320) violates.

finding.evidence: `YorkieDocStore.snapshot()` is a no-op — "Yorkie tracks undo units via doc.update()" (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) — and `applyStyles` opens its own `this.doc.update(...)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806). `Doc.setBlockType` now issues `store.setBlockType` (one update) followed by `dropStaleStyleOff` → `store.applyStyles` (a second update); `afterNamedStyleChange` (view/editor.ts:1052) does the same after `writeStylesAndRematerialize` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2686, itself documented as "a single doc.update so the whole change is one undo unit"); the paste path does it after `insertBlocks`. The new comments claim the cleanup "undoes as one step" with the caller, which holds only for `MemDocStore`'s snapshot stack — under the collaborative store the first Cmd+Z undoes only the cleanup and leaves the heading/redefinition/paste in place.

verdict.reason: All claimed facts verified. YorkieDocStore.snapshot() is a no-op (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2727-2729) and undo() delegates straight to doc.history.undo() (2731-2736), so undo granularity equals one doc.update() — a contract stated in the store interface itself ("a loop of applyStyle() calls produces one undo unit per call on stores (like YorkieDocStore) whose undo granularity is tied to the write itself", store.ts:83-89). The stale-style cleanup writes via this.store.applyStyles(edits) (document.ts:566), which opens its own this.doc.update(...) in the Yorkie store (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1806). Each caller therefore issues two updates for one user action: Doc.setBlockType does store.setBlockType (own doc.update at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1461) then dropStaleStyleOff (document.ts:606-611); afterNamedStyleChange calls dropStaleStyleOffAll after writeStylesAndRematerialize, itself a single doc.update documented as "one undo unit" (editor.ts:1052-1056; yorkie-doc-store.ts:2686,2710-2716); the internal-clipboard paste does it after insertBlocks (text-editor.ts:1258-1264). Editor undo issues exactly one docStore.undo() per Cmd+Z (editor.ts:1998). The comment claiming "the redefinition and the cleanup undo as one step" because of the caller's snapshot() (editor.ts:1049-1050) holds only for MemDocStore, whose snapshot() pushes an undo entry (memory.ts:159-162). No batching/grouping mechanism exists in YorkieDocStore to merge the two updates. This is in-lane (behaviour change breaking an invariant relied on by a consumer in another package) and blocking at major severity.
